about.title: Mammoth Lakes Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Mammoth Lakes moves at the pace of the season, and so does its traffic. Visitors unfamiliar with Old Mammoth Road or the Rt 203 corridor share the pavement with locals commuting to work along Main Street and Minaret Road, and that mix creates the conditions for collisions, particularly late in the week as afternoon traffic builds. Whether you were stopped at an intersection, merging near the village, or driving home after a shift, a crash can leave you dealing with vehicle repairs, medical appointments, and an insurance adjuster who wants a quick statement. We handle car accident claims for Mammoth Lakes residents and visitors. Our team can evaluate what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

whyChoose.title: What Matters After a Mammoth Lakes Crash

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — such as a public road authority — is involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible for the crash. Your recovery is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: Be Careful With Recorded Statements
items.desc: There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering under California law, but insurers often try to lock in a low-value recorded statement early. Speaking with us first, and preserving evidence like photos and witness contacts, protects your position before you say anything on record.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Mammoth Lakes?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as one responsible for maintaining Rt 203 or another public road, may be involved, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months. It's worth having us review your situation early so you don't miss a shorter filing window.

items.question: Does Mammoth Lakes' seasonal traffic affect my claim?
items.answer: It can. Crashes reported in Mammoth Lakes tend to cluster on Thursdays in the late afternoon, often tied to visitor traffic along corridors like Main Street and Minaret Road. That pattern doesn't change California's fault or filing rules, but it can matter for gathering witnesses and understanding how the accident happened.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with us. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what to say and help preserve evidence from the scene.
